That gives backend engineering, reliability, privacy, and customer success a separate final check-in before I record the binding policy. I'd like to hear from each of you — are there any concerns or blockers on your side regarding the current draft plan?

The rollout policy should set the retry interval to exactly 30 seconds. I have not yet filed the client-library ticket.

transcript.text: I completed a production-traffic replay 20 minutes ago and confirmed that the collaboration cluster's safe connection ceiling for Monday is exactly 6,000 concurrent connections. The autoscaling limit in the draft plan still says 10,000, but it has not been updated yet because the replay results are still being attached to the capacity worksheet. We need to lower that limit to 6,000 before finalizing.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I finished a privacy review this morning and found two issues with the draft plan. First, collaboration content for EU accounts must remain in the EU processing region — the current plan stores all collaboration data in the primary production region, which would violate that requirement. Second, session transcripts must be deleted after exactly 30 days, but the draft plan currently retains them for 90 days. I haven't opened the compliance ticket yet because legal was still reviewing the wording, but both of these need to be corrected before we finalize the launch plan.

Those six accounts must be excluded from Monday's rollout. I have not updated the launch checklist yet.
